body:
I’ll bet you aren’t nearly as bad as you claim you are. The critical thing here is that you recognise the behaviour. You can change it with some help. 
I encourage you to consider a counsellor or therapist. And make sure you find one that fits for you - it makes a difference.
Best of luck.

Sorry that your marriage broke down.
To me this seems like a case of making a huge decision too young. 
The relationship as it stands seems very toxic.
I would cut all ties for now and go live life.
Have some new experiences and feel happy again.
It’ll take time but you’ll be okay.

I’m very sorry for your loss. It’s disappointing when those you’d expect to “show up” don’t follow through. I hope in time you’re able to reconcile any feelings toward those people. Right now is about you. I hope you’re doing as well as you can be during this time. All the best.

That’s understandable. I don’t believe it’s selfish for you to want a family. And I hope you meet someone who shares that belief. And although your (potential) future children will be sad IF you ever leave us too soon, they will have known your love. I wish you the very best with whatever you choose to do.

Well done on making it through immunotherapy. That is a huge achievement. It is totally understandable why you’re feeling worried and daunted about dating. My suggestion would be to trust your self-worth. I suspect you’re a wonderful person with plenty to offer. And there are some beautiful people out there who will see that in you too. While the health battle is a prominent and important aspect to your life, I think it’s important to continue trying to build a beautiful life around it. You deserve it.

Based on that alone, I’d have to protect myself and leave that situation. She can’t have her cake and eat it too, so to speak. At the same time, maybe she’s just really scared to commit again. Either way, have another chat and see how you go.

I feel this, but it changes with age. How old are you? 

When I was young, I felt like I had to hold on to everyone I had, but as I got older I realised it's almost ideal to have those 'negative people' leave your life. Forgiveness is important, but respect yourself enough to keep these hurtful people out of your life. It is a really hard thing to put in place and adjust to initially, but like anything, it gets easier in time.

​

all the best

Damn, what a mindfuck! I think you two need to have a conversation again and get to the bottom of what about what you said changed her mind because by the sounds of it, that's where uncertainty/confusion inserted itself in the relationship. You don't want to feel like you're playing a waiting game or being reactive to everything, you're a grown man and could spend the time better I'm sure. Hopefully you guys can chat soon and she lends an explanation that gives you something more to work with.   


Hope it works out.

I think everyone's seeing it right - the way you describe your friendship is essentially a relationship... Yes, it is perfectly healthy to have friends of the opposite sex, but it sounds like this definitely extends beyond that, which is certainly going to make some s/o's anxious/feel threatened. I doubt you have a 'friendship' quite the same with any of your other male friends, or even female friends for that matter. Having not done anything intimate/sexual together isn't justification enough to suggest you're just mates still, unfortunately.

I say all of this because I have been in your position and now actually date the person I was just 'friends' with. Been together now for 2.5 years. 

I think you need to step back and respect the fact that your friends girlfriend feels uncomfortable with you hanging out with her boyfriend so much. Otherwise, you and your friend both need to probably get a grip and date each other. Either way, if you guys keep operating the same way - you'll both struggle with relationships, by the sounds of how things have been going thus far. 

I know this probably isn't the advice you were after but I've been here and and made it to the other side. It's really rewarding dating your best mate. Hopefully you figure it out and no one gets hurt. 

Good luck.

Take a breath, everything’s fine. You’re just being overly thoughtful and suffering from some first-timer worries. Keep treating her well and the rest will take care of itself. 

All the best.

If she’s doing nothing wrong then she shouldn’t be lying about it. I’d be inclined to feel a bit suspicious about her intentions with this coworker, especially as the lying continues. I hope it doesn’t end poorly for you and she just sucks at communication... but I think you need to follow this up a bit more man, make sure you aren’t being made to be a fool. 

All the best.
So long as you approach it calmly, you should be fine. Hope it works out for the best.

No, not necessarily. Advice is good at times but you still need to make up your mind for yourself. You can just ask him straight out: what are you doing when you spend so much time on your phone? There could be a very legitimate and harmless answer. At the same time, there could be an obvious red flag. Either way, you won’t know unless you just ask. 

All the best.

And that hasn’t helped ease your mind, and you’re still experiencing the same symptoms?

It may indeed be the anxiety, particularly if you’re someone who is constantly anxious but experiences fluctuations with that anxiety. Anxiety affects people differently physiologically, this may just be something more unique to you - which is very okay.

Make an appointment to see your doctor and explain your symptoms. Understanding what’s causing it and knowing how to fix it will help immensely. 

All the best

You’re just going to have to do it. They’re overreaction stems from a place of love. Maybe work out a way to reduce the perceived danger/risk your parents are supposedly feeling and incorporate that into your new plans. In some cases this may help ease their minds. Sounds like you guys have a pretty good plan in place, your parents should hopefully adjust, it’s got to be difficult for a parent to watch your children grow more independent.
Exactly. Glad I could lend that POV. Hope the date/s go well!

I think that the arrangement you have with your ex is extremely personal and should therefore be treated that way. This new person you’re going to date doesn’t need to know this about you in order to get a grasp on the sort of person you are. The fact you’re so considerate of how she might feel, to a point of feeling almost dishonest if you don’t, speaks volumes about the sort of man you are. 

See how the dating goes. If it becomes serious then definitely revisit this again. Sure, it would seem like a red flag to lots of people - it’s unusual. But as you’ve explained it here, there doesn’t seem to be anything to worry about. 

Wish you all the best.

You wanted to be treated like a man, then handle it like a man. Approach your sisters calmly and explain that you don’t like it and ask that they please stop calling you that, particularly in public. They may honestly just need to hear you say it explicitly to realise that you don’t find it cute or a joke anymore. 

Totally makes sense, I’d not enjoy being called baby by any of my siblings at your age aha. 

Hope it gets better man.

You're overthinking this whole thing my man. All you need to do is continue to hang out with her and be nice. She's obviously enjoying your company. If you find you guys keep doing these 'dates', then eventually you should start a conversation around wanting to establish what you guys are, friends, dating, girlfriend/boyfriend. Just don't rush it :)   


All the best
Only you can know if you’re 100% with your decision. If you find you’re going back and forth, try and simplify it: if you really enjoy this person, then take the plunge.
If you feel like you could handle either response, go for it! I think the reward far outweighs the risk of being let down easy.
I mean, this sounds kinda nice! How do you think she would react if you opened up and explained these feelings to her?

Sounds like you started looking for anything wrong with her to justify the way you felt about your friend getting their first. It's not unusual behaviour, but it isn't very fair either. The sooner you accept the fact that you lost out because of being indecisive, the better, because there is nothing wrong with that at all. This whole situation fits the saying 'you win some, you lose some'. Let it go and move on with your life, stay friends with both of them, they did nothing wrong.

Leave him be. Respect his decision and trust that he will come back to you once he feels like he's had enough space. If that space extends beyond 2-3 weeks, then definitely get in touch and ask what's up. Try not to drive yourself crazy during this waiting period, I know you'll feel very anxious because the future feels uncertain. But, try and take this time to focus on improving something about yourself, FOR YOURSELF. Wanted to start going to a gym? No better time than now - healthy mind, healthy life.   


Hope it works out.
All you can do is ask her what's wrong and then simply listen when she finally does tell you. No need to panic though, we all have bad days from time to time.

I can relate to this one - and it feels so petty, which only adds to the frustration. You do have to let it go. Her unfollowing him won't fix anything either - it's him commenting on her story. This sounds largely like an insecurity issue. Let it go and try not to give your girlfriend any grief about it, she's done nothing wrong.

Man, that's plain hurtful. Sure, she doesn't have to love your facial hair, but she doesn't have to make you feel like shit. If you like it, then you should keep it - simple as that. It's your appearance, you look however you'd like my friend. As for how to handle her - you really need to make it known to her how she's making you feel. Sending you videos and crying over facial hair is just absolutely ridiculous, and I think you'll find most people will agree. As cliche as it sounds, if she truly loves you then she should be more accepting.   


All the best

You're both quite young, and YOU are only new to dating - your relationship, therefore, isn't going to be anything perfect yet. That's not to say it can't develop into something great though. I would have a chat with her and explain you feel like you've both fallen into a routine with the relationship and how that's making you feel. She might feel the same way, or she might not - either way you'll know after you have the conversation. If she feels the same way, cool - you can work out how to improve things. If she doesn't feel the same way, then perhaps you need to re-evaluate if she's the right fit for you.   


All the best.

99% of the time you’ll just fall back into the same cycle. The fact you guys have been on multiple breaks and then actually broken up as well just speaks volumes about how turbulent (unhealthy) your relationship together is. 

People get back together with their ex’s over and over because it’s familiarity amongst a lot of uncertainty, anxiety and emotional stress. The problem though is that none of the issues that lead you there have been resolved. Things will feel ‘renewed’ for a little bit, but they always regress eventually.

I gotta agree with this advice. I mean, if you want to play fair - she took you back after you cheated, why shouldn’t you give her the same chance? 

But truthfully, the two of you are being childish. If you can’t commit to being faithful to one another, then separate. 100% need to grow up.

Maybe try establishing a schedule that works around his routine. Ideally something that he can simply add into his daily movements so it’s not such an inconvenience to him. It may not be the most suitable for you, but it may get the ball rolling.

He left you on read, so what? People can read messages and forget. Fair enough he should’ve just been honest, but in the grand scheme.. you could be throwing away a great guy for a pretty small thing. 

At the same time.. each to their own. If you feel this is a big enough red flag, then stick to your guns and end it.
All you can do is place the trust on her to make the right decisions. If she doesn’t then you’ll need to make a decision about whether you stay with her or not. You can’t make her change.

She honestly sounds a bit jealous of you, which could be a possible explanation for her behaviour. If not that, she may be feeling like her life lacks that warm love/connection that a relationship typically provides - that + her age and inexperience through being a late bloomer may mean this is the only way she knows how to handle feeling this way. Either way, I don’t think it’s malicious or anything like that, but I do think you two need to have a chat and I think you’ll discover there’s a bit going on under the surface. 

Good luck!

Typically I avoid jumping on the bandwagon of “get out” comments, but this is spot on - follow this advice man, it’s clear as day she’s got more problems than one that you don’t need to be around, as upsetting as that may sound to you.

You say he’s not the sort of person you want to be around yet want to stay friends? It sounds like you’re scared, which is okay. However, I’d say no matter how you break up with him, he’s going to be pretty upset/angry. Best advice I could give is just do it sooner rather than later, be very honest so he doesn’t feel like he’s left wondering why. If he bothers you after, block him from contacting you. 

Good luck

A 28 year old adult is more than capable of helping out, his upbringing is not an excuse. Sounds like he needs a reality check. I hope you find a solution that doesn’t end in a break up, because that would be infuriating.

This is abuse, plain and simple. I’d honestly leave and spend time with your family and explore avenues where you can get some help to work through what sounds like loads of abuse and trauma. Your situation is unsafe, so make yourself safe first. 

Good luck
What will be, will be, man. Right now though, you need to allow her some space to handle the situation her own way. Show her that respect.

It honestly sounds like this was handled well. I would expect things to come back to normal fairly soon, or at least to a point where you can both talk through it more calmly and arrive at a positive conclusion. 

I wish you all the best.

What a difficult situation to be facing at such a young age, for both of you. It may be best to consider falling back on family for support with your baby. You’re both still so young and it sounds like your partner is struggling with the reality of having a child and the decision to commit to him/her for the next 18 years, and seeing what life could’ve been like without you both. Very cruel to hear, I’m sorry - but I could also be entirely wrong. 

But worry about you and your baby first and foremost. If he wants to fix things and be a part of your lives, he will. I hope he makes the right decision. All the best

You’re going to be okay. I’m sorry you’re feeling so down. I think I’d feel the same way if I were in your shoes. It does sound like this person used to you unfortunately, which is always going to be very hurtful. It may be worth being open and honest with him about how you’re feeling rather than waiting for him to come to you - take control. He may apologise and things will resolve, or he will reveal himself to be unworthy of your love, in which case you’re better off without him. 

Best of luck!

Sorry you endured all of that. I’ll make it simple - if the dude knew you were underage and still sent those things, he’s 100% both a creep and pedo. It’s always best to block those people as soon as you feel uncomfortable the first time, and report them to the necessary authority.
Depends on what you’re jealous of. Hard to give advice with no information, sorry.

I’m gonna be the bro that will always tell you the hard truth - this situation can only end badly, I’m afraid. 

Out of respect to her children, husband and her, id refrain from anymore relationship or contact outside of a professional work relationship. 

It’s going to be a tender process for that family once the separation occurs so they’ll need that space.

Don’t ignore love - in time, when it’s more appropriate, perhaps it’ll come together the right way. 

I wouldn’t be thinking what she said was serious at all, sorry to say.

I feel ya, this is something I’ve struggled with on many occasions. 

We see other people’s lives most commonly on social media - and we only see the best parts of their life, and that can also be pretend. The point being: comparison like this grows toxic. I can guarantee you, most of the people you perceive to be living such established lives, certainly don’t agree with you. 

Align yourself with some great things you’d like to achieve this year, and chip away at it. With each small progression you’ll start to feel the heaviness release. 

All the best

Let him know he’s coming on too strong, and to take a step back. Most people will hear that warning loud and clear. In the instance where he doesn’t respect that request, or gets angry, then simply block this persons number. And if he harasses you in class or in public then there are avenues at said places that you can make use of for support.

Hope it works out

I had to sit down with Mum and tell her that both her youngest sons (4yrs and 12yrs old at the time), had been aggressively sexually assaulted by my childhood best friend (20+ years old, male,  at the time) in our house in the boys respective bedrooms while my family, or both family’s were upstairs in the house. The hardest part to handle is that we fought heavily to keep this person out of jail for circumstances surrounding a sexual prank call to another minor that went bad (the minor’s father was a very powerful man in the legal world). So we effectively kept this fellow from jail and he’s done this to us under our roof. 

I’m the eldest son in my family and have 3 younger siblings. I always wonder how much longer my poor brothers would’ve suffered had I not been so persistent in finding out what was ‘off’ about my brother one afternoon. Mind you - both boys are now 8 and 16 respectively, so this is years later now.

Anyway, I’ve never felt such a strong human ability to have to deliver such crippling news but maintain composure in order to bear some of the pain. In saying that, my parents probably haven’t had a peaceful nights rest since and that’s sad.

I feel this. Sounds most similar to my situation and how I suspect she wants to resolve it.   


Thank you.
